title: Beyond the Solar System
summary: Stars, galaxies and the Milky Way, light years and huge distances, how we look into space with telescopes, and South Africa's role in astronomy.

notes.text: The sun is just one of billions of stars. Stars differ in **size**, **temperature** and **colour**: blue stars are the hottest, then white, yellow (like the sun), orange, and red stars, which are the coolest. Stars look tiny because they are extremely far away.

items: A **constellation** is a group of stars that forms a pattern in the night sky, such as Orion or Crux (the Southern Cross).
The **Southern Cross** and its two pointer stars help people in the southern hemisphere find south at night.
Many cultures gave names to stars. In isiXhosa, the Pleiades star cluster is *isiLimela*; its appearance marked the start of the planting season.

notes.text: A huge system of billions of stars, gas and dust held together by gravity.

Our solar system is in the **Milky Way**, a **spiral galaxy** about 100 000 light years across. On a dark, clear night it appears as a faint band of light across the sky. The nearest large galaxy is **Andromeda**. From the southern hemisphere you can see two small nearby galaxies, the **Large and Small Magellanic Clouds**. The **universe** contains billions of galaxies.

notes.text: The DISTANCE light travels in one year: about 9,5 million million km (9,5 × 10¹² km). It is a unit of distance, not time.

rows: Proxima Centauri (nearest star after the sun)

notes.label: Remember
notes.text: When we look at a distant star we see light that left it long ago. Light from the sun is about 8 minutes old; light from Andromeda left it 2,5 million years ago. Looking far into space means looking back in time.

items: **Optical telescopes** use lenses or mirrors to collect visible light. Large ones are built on high mountains or in dry, dark places away from city lights.
**Radio telescopes** use large dishes to collect radio waves from space; they work in cloudy weather and in daylight.
**Space telescopes** such as Hubble and James Webb orbit above the atmosphere, which blurs and blocks some radiation.
Space probes and rovers travel to planets and send back pictures and data.

notes.text: South Africa's clear, dark skies make it one of the best places in the world for astronomy. **SALT** (the Southern African Large Telescope) near Sutherland in the Northern Cape is the largest single optical telescope in the southern hemisphere. **MeerKAT**, a radio telescope of 64 dishes in the Karoo, is part of the international **Square Kilometre Array (SKA)** project, which will be the world's largest radio telescope.
Space exploration has given us satellites for communication, weather forecasting and GPS navigation, as well as inventions such as improved water filters and medical imaging.

questions.prompt: Explain what astronomers mean when they say that looking at distant galaxies is looking back in time.
questions.memo:
✓ Light takes a very long time (millions of years) to travel from distant galaxies to Earth (1)
✓ so we see the galaxy as it was when the light left it, not as it is now (1)
